headline: MIN-DEGREE EXTRACTION IS SEALED (Attack03.exists_minDegree_of_card_edgeFinset). Every finite graph with more than k*n edges has a NONEMPTY vertex set T on which every vertex has more than k neighbours inside T. Proved by the classical deletion argument, by strong induction on |S|, with no Nat-subtraction anywhere: the deletion identity sum_degIn_erase says deleting v removes EXACTLY 2 * degIn G S v from the degree sum, and nat_descent does the arithmetic with the nonlinear product 2*k*|S| abstracted to an opaque atom so omega sees a linear problem. This is item (a) of the two lemmas Attack01's TERMINAL named as missing for ConjectureAt 1.

THE CONCLUSION IS STATED IN THE SPEC'S OWN VOCABULARY, ON PURPOSE. The degree floor is `k < (G.neighborSet v INTER (coe T)).ncard` - VERBATIM the shape the frozen spec's IsDegenerate uses. So the extraction's conclusion is the exact negation of the witness IsDegenerate demands at the set (coe T), and the two compose with no glue. Attack03.ncard_neighborSet_inter is the bridge, and it is the reason §5 below is three lines rather than a development.

r-DEGENERATE GRAPHS ARE SPARSE, MACHINE-CHECKED (Attack03.IsDegenerate.card_edgeFinset_le): IsDegenerate r H implies #E(H) <= r * |V(H)|. Proved by contraposition against the extraction, from the spec's own definition of IsDegenerate and nothing else. This is the FIRST QUANTITATIVE consequence of the degeneracy hypothesis in this campaign - every earlier result about the hypothesis (Attack02.degeneracy_hierarchy_strict and friends) was structural. The relative form IsDegenerate.sum_degIn_le bounds the degree sum inside EVERY vertex subset by 2*r*|S|, which is the form an induction along a degeneracy order consumes.

THREE SHAPES OF THE WITNESS ARE BANKED, DELIBERATELY. Finset-relative (exists_minDegree_aux / exists_minDegree_subset, which hands back a concrete T SUBSET S plus the degree floor on it - what a greedy embedding consumes); Mathlib edge-count global (exists_minDegree_of_card_edgeFinset, bridged by Mathlib's own handshake lemma sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges, not a re-derivation); and an honest SimpleGraph.Subgraph object (exists_subgraph_minDegree, on (TOP : G.Subgraph).induce (coe T), with verts = coe T proved by rfl and the neighbourhood transported by neighborSet_induce_top).

REUSABLE ACROSS EVERY DEGENERATE-TURAN TARGET. Attack03 mentions neither bipartiteness nor H nor ex(n;-). It is a statement about an arbitrary finite SimpleGraph and a natural number k. Nothing in it is specific to Erdos 146.
open: ConjectureAt 2 (Conjecture_r_two) - UNTOUCHED. Nothing in this campaign bears on its truth.
Conjecture, ConjectureAt r for r >= 1 - UNTOUCHED.

ConjectureAt 1 - NOT PROVED. Of the two lemmas Attack01's TERMINAL named, (a) MIN-DEGREE EXTRACTION is now CLOSED by Attack03. (b) GREEDY EMBEDDING remains untouched and was deliberately not attempted here: given the degeneracy order of Attack01.exists_degeneracyList for a 1-degenerate H on h vertices and a graph of minimum degree >= h, construct a term of SimpleGraph.Copy H G by placing vertices in reverse list order, each attaching to at most 1 already-placed vertex. It is a term-construction by induction along a list, a multi-hundred-line development, and it does not belong in the same file as the extraction.

EVEN WITH (b), ConjectureAt 1 IS NOT IMMEDIATE. The extraction plus the embedding give the containment step; turning that into a bound on ex(n;H) with a Vinogradov constant still has to be assembled, and no part of that assembly exists in this campaign.
The spec's convention (1) counterexample (P4 vs K_{n/2,n/2}, showing the INDUCED reading of the conjecture is false) - not formalized. It needs a lower bound on an induced-Turan number.

The spec's convention (9) claim (a single Vinogradov constant working for all H at once is false) - not formalized. It needs Kovari-Sos-Turan-type LOWER bounds on ex(n; K_{r,r}), which this campaign has no machinery for.

obstructionMap.conclusionAxis: CLOSED as an obstruction (Attack01). scale is strictly increasing in r under <<; any attempt to reach ConjectureAt r from a weaker exponent is refuted at the level of the bound itself.
obstructionMap.hypothesisAxis: CLOSED as an obstruction (Attack02). K_{r,r} witnesses strictness of IsDegenerate inside the bipartite class. Attack03 adds the QUANTITATIVE arm of the same axis: IsDegenerate r now implies #E <= r*n, so the hypothesis is no longer only a structural predicate.
obstructionMap.reductionAxis: PARTIALLY OPEN, unchanged by Attack03. Universe quantifier eliminated (conjectureAt_of_fin). Edge-maximality reduction available. The r=0 conjunct proved free. What remains unreduced is the quantifier over m and over graphs on Fin m.
obstructionMap.constructiveAxis: HALF CLOSED. Attack01's TERMINAL put both missing lemmas here. Extraction is now sealed (Attack03). Greedy embedding is the whole of what remains on this axis, and it is where the r=1 case now lives entirely. Nothing in this campaign still produces an upper bound on ex(n;H) better than the trivial n^2 (Attack01.exR_vinogradov_sq), and Attack01.distance_to_target proves that trivial bound is strictly insufficient.

next_command: GREEDY EMBEDDING, its own campaign, its own budget. Build a term of SimpleGraph.Copy H G by induction along the list from Attack01.exists_degeneracyList: for a 1-degenerate H on h vertices and a G whose minimum degree exceeds h, each vertex added in reverse list order has at most 1 already-placed neighbour, so a free neighbour of that neighbour's image always exists inside the extracted set T of Attack03.exists_minDegree_subset (whose degree floor is stated in exactly that usable form). Do NOT budget this at 8 kernel iterations; it is a term construction, not a tactic proof, and the induction hypothesis has to carry the injectivity of the partial embedding.

headline: AKS IS INSUFFICIENT, MACHINE-CHECKED (Attack01.aks_bound_insufficient). For every r >= 1 there is an explicit f satisfying the cited AKS conclusion VinogradovLE f (scale (4*r)) and REFUTING VinogradovLE f (scale r). So no derivation consuming `alon_krivelevich_sudakov` as a black box can prove ConjectureAt r. The spec's prose claim that the exponent gap IS the open problem is now a theorem.

THE UNIVERSE IS NOT PART OF THE PROBLEM (Attack01.conjectureAt_of_fin / conjectureAt_fin_iff). Proving the bound for bipartite r-degenerate graphs on Fin m, for every m, proves ConjectureAt.{u} r in EVERY universe u; at u=0 it is an iff. A mechanised attack may work entirely with Fin-indexed graphs.

BOTH AXES MOVE STRICTLY, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Conclusion axis (Attack01.scale_not_vinogradov): scale s is never << scale r for r < s. Hypothesis axis (Attack02.degeneracy_hierarchy_strict): K_{r,r} is bipartite, r-degenerate, and NOT k-degenerate for any k < r. More graphs, weaker bound - so no ConjectureAt k implies any other, and r=2 is genuinely its own problem.

A DEGENERACY ORDER EXISTS (Attack01.exists_degeneracyList). Every finite r-degenerate graph has a vertex list in which each vertex has at most r neighbours among those still to come. Read backwards this is the greedy-embedding order - the input the r=1 proof needs.
open: ConjectureAt 2 (Conjecture_r_two) - UNTOUCHED. Nothing in this campaign bears on its truth.
Conjecture, ConjectureAt r for r >= 1 - UNTOUCHED.

ConjectureAt 1 - NOT PROVED, though the target is now visible. Two lemmas are missing and neither was attempted: (a) MIN-DEGREE EXTRACTION - a finite graph G with #E(G) > k * #V(G) has a nonempty vertex subset whose induced subgraph has minimum degree > k (proved by repeatedly deleting a vertex of degree <= k; the invariant e > k*v survives each deletion, and forces nonemptiness at the end); (b) GREEDY EMBEDDING - given the degeneracy order of Attack01.exists_degeneracyList for a 1-degenerate H on h vertices and a graph G of minimum degree >= h, build a SimpleGraph.Copy H G by placing vertices in reverse list order, each attaching to at most 1 already-placed vertex. (b) is the expensive half: it constructs a term of Copy by induction along a list and is a multi-hundred-line development, not a budget-8 job.
The spec's convention (1) counterexample (P4 vs K_{n/2,n/2}, showing the INDUCED reading of the conjecture is false) - not formalized. It needs a lower bound on an induced-Turan number.

The spec's convention (9) claim (a single Vinogradov constant working for all H at once is false) - not formalized. It needs Kovari-Sos-Turan-type LOWER bounds on ex(n; K_{r,r}), which this campaign has no machinery for.

Any future attempt to reach ConjectureAt r from a weaker exponent is refuted at the level of the bound itself, before any graph theory.
obstructionMap.hypothesisAxis: CLOSED as an obstruction. K_{r,r} witnesses strictness of IsDegenerate inside the bipartite class.

The r=0 conjunct proved free (conjectureAt_zero, conjecture_iff_ge_one). What remains unreduced is the quantifier over m and over graphs on Fin m.
obstructionMap.constructiveAxis: OPEN. This is where the remaining work is: min-degree extraction and greedy embedding (see `open` above). Nothing in this campaign produces an upper bound on ex(n;H) better than the trivial n^2 (Attack01.exR_vinogradov_sq), and Attack01.distance_to_target proves that trivial bound is strictly insufficient. The entire content of the target lies in that gap, and the gap is untouched.
